- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends — forecasts dip too late or too slowly.
- Overreacts to recent price spikes, overshooting the true value by 2–5% in the immediate aftermath.
- Underestimates mean-reversion periods — fails to recognize when prices are “stuck” near a support level and should not rise sharply.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is above 70–72, suggesting model is not calibrated to recent high volatility regimes.
- When true price rises >5% from prior day, model often fails to capture the full magnitude, especially in the first 5 days of forecast.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust quickly to sudden drops or spikes, leading to persistent lag or overshoot in the middle of the forecast window.
